name: Triplit
tagline: Full-stack syncing database for TypeScript apps; development has stalled since 2025.
description: Triplit is a TypeScript database that runs both in the client (IndexedDB or memory) and on a server (SQLite, Durable Objects and others), syncing over websockets with optimistic local writes, relational-style queries with includes, schemas and role-based permissions. It aimed to give React, Vue, Svelte and Solid apps realtime, offline-capable data without writing a backend. Its last npm release was in July 2025, and co-founder Matt Linkous joined Supabase in October 2025 to work on sync integrations. The AGPL code remains on GitHub with little activity, so treat it as stalled.
statusNote: No releases since July 2025; co-founder joined Supabase (Oct 2025) and the project website was unreachable during verification. Code stays AGPL on GitHub.

pricing.notes: Self-hosted server is free under AGPL; hosted offering status unclear.

strengths: Same query API on client and server with optimistic local writes
Relational includes and schemas with role-based permissions
Pluggable storage from IndexedDB to SQLite and Durable Objects
weaknesses: Development has stalled; no releases since mid-2025
AGPL license is a hurdle for some commercial deployments
Small community and uncertain hosted offering
useCases: Learning or prototyping local-first sync patterns
notIdealFor: New production projects needing an active vendor
Large datasets or high write throughput
